 Sunday Beach and Boating Forecast 
 Rip Current Risk: Moderate Lightning Risk: None 
 By Mike Modrick Published : Oct. 25, 2026 at 4:37 AM EDT | Updated : 16 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SARASOTA, Fla. (WWSB) - 🏖️ Sunday Beach Forecast - WINDY 
 Rip Current Risk: Moderate Lightning Risk: None 
 Siesta Key (Siesta Key) Head to the Suncoast beaches Sunday for some sunshine and pleasant weather! It’ll be sunny with temperatures in the low 80s, and the water is cooling into the upper 70s. The northeast wind will be around 20 to 30 mph, with higher gusts. There’s a moderate rip current risk, so swim near lifeguards and be aware of water conditions. The UV index is high, so don’t forget your sunscreen. Hang on to the beach umbrella and plan to chase your beach gear as it blows down the sand. 
 ⛵ Suncoast Boating Forecast – Small Craft Advisories in Effect thru Wednesday 
 Boating Forecast (Boating Forecast) Northeast winds will continue over the Suncoast waters through the next week, creating advisory-level conditions that boaters need to respect. A tightening pressure gradient is driving these persistent winds, and conditions will remain challenging for the next several days before gradually moderating.
 Sunday: Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots, increasing to 25 to 30 knots in the afternoon. Bay and inland waters will be very rough. Small craft advisory conditions are in effect.
 Monday: Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots with gusts up to 30 knots. Bay and inland waters remain rough. Small craft advisory continues.
 Tuesday: Northeast winds 15 to 20 knots with gusts up to 25 knots. Conditions begin to ease slightly, with bay and inland waters becoming choppy rather than rough.
 Wednesday: Northeast winds 15 to 20 knots. Bay and inland waters are choppy. Conditions continue to moderate as the system moves away.
 The Small Craft Advisory will likely remain in effect through at least Wednesday.
 Tropical Outlook (Tropical Outlook) TROPICAL OUTLOOK - NEXT 7 DAYS 
 The National Hurricane Center is not expecting any tropical cyclone formation over the next seven days across the North Atlantic, Caribbean Sea, or Gulf.
